evidence.detail: run() does no time-gating: it always processes prices if n < TOTAL_RUNS and the rotation window is open; there is no check of when the last run file was written
rotation.files() returns sorted list of Run_N.txt files; os.path.getmtime on the last entry gives elapsed time since most recent run
TOTAL_RUNS = 168, so runs should be spaced ~1 hour apart over 7 days; detecting 'due' means checking if mtime of latest file is > ~55 minutes ago

triage.fix_sketch: In rotation_script/rotation_script.py:run(), after the n==0 early-return block (~line 50), add: if files exist, check os.path.getmtime(files[-1]); if fewer than 3300 seconds (55 min) have elapsed, print 'Run not due, skipping' and return. This keeps the script idempotent when called frequently. Separately, update the external scheduler (cron/systemd) to invoke the script every 5 minutes instead of every hour. No schema change, no data change, under 10 lines.
triage.notes: bakert's comment already outlines the approach (run every 5 mins, only write a file if an hour has passed). The code change is isolated to rotation_script.py and is fully reversible.
